cls2-cpsb-250.why: COST_PER_STATE_BYTE 1530->250 (a CHEAPER reprice): a fresh slot falls to 2,100+10,000+16,000 = 28,100, so the 30,000 and 50,000 sub-floor budgets become write-capable and archetype 2's 'cannot create state' arm must fail

cls12-cold-read-5000.why: COLD_STORAGE_ACCESS 2100->5000 (reads get DEARER, EIP-1884-shaped): a capable probe target at the 5,000 literal stops answering, and ERC-7579 postCheck's 3,229-gas read-only body no longer fits

cls12-cold-read-700.why: COLD_STORAGE_ACCESS 2100->700 (reads get CHEAPER, EIP-1108-scale 3x cut): an overrunning target now fits both probe literals and answers 'yes', so an incapable target is read as capable

cls2-storage-set-osaka-60000.why: pre-8037 STORAGE_SET 20000->60000: the pre-EIP-8037 slot floor rises to 62,100, so the 30,000 and 50,000 budgets lose the write capability archetype 2 pins them as having on those forks

cls3-cold-storage-write-4500.why: pre-8037 COLD_STORAGE_WRITE 5000->4500: the cold total EIP-2929 deliberately preserved moves, so the hardcoded-5000 equality for a replacing write stops holding. Isolates the reset term from STORAGE_SET, which this does not touch

cls3-storage-write-9000.why: Amsterdam STORAGE_WRITE 10000->9000: the execution part of every storage write moves, so both post-8037 charges (110,020 creating and 12,100 replacing) move with it

cls2-storage-set-osaka-1000.why: pre-8037 STORAGE_SET 20000->1000 (a CHEAPER reprice): the slot floor falls to 3,100, below ERC-7579 postCheck's 3,229, so the one budget that was never write-capable becomes write-capable
